about: How many signatures a candidate's petition for a municipal office asks, as the place's law scales it to the town, where data/research/elections/filing-requirements.json (municipalOffice rows) gives a percentage, a floor, a ceiling or a count by town size. Read by petitionRule in src/core2/modules/elections.ts and applied to the town's own voters by petitionNeededHere in src/core2/modules/voting.ts. The research rows for municipalities are state general-law defaults marked estimate, so every row here is ESTIMATED from that row's own text (quoted in `text`). A state or side with no row here keeps what its research row gives: a fixed count, none, or the median of the read counts (SG-GOV-petition-count-estimated). A side with no row of its own reads the party row, as in the research file.
share: The fraction of the base the law asks. `base` is "registered" (registered voters) or "votes" (votes cast for the office or at the last election); the world keeps no voter rolls, so a registered base is the town's eligible voters times registeredShareOfEligible and a votes base the town's people times localElectorateShareOfPopulation (both in campaigns/parameters.json; the latter is a presidential year's, so it overstates a local election's); where the world has recorded the office's last election, a "votes" base reads those votes.

fields.min: floor on the count, where the law sets one
fields.max: ceiling on the count, where the law sets one
fields.orFixed: the count when the law says the fixed number or the share, whichever is less
fields.byPopulation: fixed counts by the town's population: the first tier whose belowPopulation exceeds the town's applies; the tier without belowPopulation is for larger towns

party.text: 5% to 10% of the vote for the office at the last city election (by charter; general-law default)
at least 25 eligible electors (10 in towns of fewer than 2,000)

independent.text: 1% of votes cast for the office at the last election (minimum about 25 in small towns)
5% of registered voters (independent in partisan cities)

party.text: 2% of votes cast for the office at the last regular city election, minimum 10 (Iowa Code 45.1)

independent.text: 2% of the last secretary of state vote in the city

party.text: town offices: 1% of votes for governor in the town, minimum 20, maximum 50
5% of the island's registered voters or 100, whichever is less
10% of the votes cast for the office at the last election, maximum 300 (city)
50 party voters, or 5% of the party's last Assembly vote, whichever is less (N.J.S.A. 19:23-8)

independent.text: 1% of votes cast for the General Assembly in the town

party.text: 5% of enrolled party voters, capped by statute (city council outside NYC: 500)

independent.text: 5% of the last gubernatorial vote, capped (the cap is the party row's 500)

party.text: 50 for city council in most cities; 10 for villages (a municipality of 5,000 people is a city, Ohio Revised Code 703.01)

independent.text: 2% of the largest vote in the municipality

party.text: 1% to 5% of the votes cast at the last municipal election; minimum 10
30 voters or 1% of the town's voters, whichever is less
